title: Monitor trademark / handle availability
summary: Monitor trademark conflicts and social-handle availability for the brand, on a schedule.

parts.title: Run the federal trademark search and social-handle checks
parts.guidance: Search the relevant brand names and variants in the official trademark tools and check the requested social handles. Record potentially conflicting marks and the terms searched so counsel can assess coverage. Handle availability and trademark clearance are separate findings. Present the available handles and flagged marks without reserving accounts, contacting owners or treating a clean exact-name search as legal clearance.

parts.title: Choose a trademark watch service (or counsel) for conflicts
parts.guidance: Define the marks, territories, classes and conflicts the watch needs to cover. Compare a specialist service and counsel-led review on coverage, alert quality, cost and how matches are evaluated. Choose the service and obtain the company’s approval for the engagement. Set a named recipient for alerts and an escalation route for potential conflicts before monitoring begins.

parts.title: Schedule the recurring monitor and alerting
parts.guidance: Configure the agreed marks, platforms and review schedule, routing alerts to the brand or legal contact. Include enough source context to inspect the match and distinguish duplicates. Test notification delivery and decide how unavailable sources are flagged. Review actual alerts before any opposition, outreach or purchase is considered; those actions need their own authorized decision.

metadata.supportReason: Trademark and handle checks run over search APIs — an agent can schedule the recurring monitor.

geoNotes.summary: Monitoring is on the owner: watch the public search portal and the weekly Trade Marks Journal — oppositions run for 4 months from publication of a conflicting application.
geoNotes.actionLabel: IP India — trade mark public search

geoNotes.summary: The UK IPO notifies owners of earlier UK marks when a similar application publishes, but acting is on you: a 2-month opposition window (extendable by one) from publication in the journal.
geoNotes.actionLabel: UK IPO — search for a trade mark

geoNotes.summary: The DPMA examines only absolute grounds and does not notify earlier owners — watching DPMAregister (or paying a watch service) is on you, with a 3-month opposition window after publication.
The INPI does not police conflicts for you: monitor the Bulletin officiel de la propriété industrielle via INPI's databases and oppose within 2 months of a conflicting publication.
INPI examines absolute grounds and publishes applications in its bulletin — watching for conflicting marks is on you (or a watch service), with a two-month opposition window from publication.
Watch the Canadian Trademarks Database for conflicting filings — CIPO does not police your mark for you — and oppositions run on a two-month window from advertisement in the Trademarks Journal.
